subject.title: feat: agent-initiated context injection (beyond user-message-triggered auto-recall)

question: Should OpenClaw support automatic non-user-triggered recall, and if so should the first supported form be an explicit retrieval tool, a memory-plugin lifecycle hook, or a core step-boundary hook?
rationale: The request is a new capability with materially different token, isolation, API, and plugin-ownership tradeoffs; source evidence supplied here does not select a safe default.

options.title: Start with explicit retrieval
options.body: Provide an opt-in, agent-invoked retrieval path first so relevance and token use remain under the agent or workflow owner's control.

options.title: Define a plugin lifecycle hook
options.body: Add a narrowly documented lifecycle seam only if the current plugin API cannot express the needed boundary without core policy.

options.title: Adopt automatic step injection
options.body: Support automatic injection only with a maintainer-approved relevance budget, isolation policy, and upgrade contract.

recommendation.title: Start with explicit retrieval
recommendation.body: Provide an opt-in, agent-invoked retrieval path first so relevance and token use remain under the agent or workflow owner's control.

likelyOwner.reason: No attributable feature-history owner was available in the supplied review context; the decision should be routed to the current active-memory and agent-lifecycle owners.
